title: THE UNKINDEST CUT
author: Mandakini Bhattacharjee
text:
Even a cut on a finger is a mandarin
teaching you several things.

How you cannot believe the hurt at first,
cannot believe you have been so stupid,
so naive, as to actually cut yourself?

Then you grow finicky at the hurt,
feeling around it, pressing it,
checking the extent to which it can hurt you - trying the boundaries.
Then you luxuriate in the pain and the pulse -
sometimes even blessing it with tears -
feeling you are the Queen of your tragedy,
feeling that invisible crown or halo.
You feed on the pain, the burst,
the grind of cleaning and dressing it,
depending on how deeply you are cut.
Then, as the scab grows back, you feel brave -
rather a hero - `cause the hurt no longer hurts -
and the scar becomes beautiful —

Till one day it disappears - and only lingers in a memory -
and then that goes away too.

Love is just such a cut on a finger.
